questions.question: Direct materials R200 000 and direct labour R150 000. Prime cost is…
Prime cost R350 000 and factory overheads R100 000. Total manufacturing cost is…
Partly finished goods are ______-in-progress.
questions.memo: Unfinished goods are work-in-progress.

questions.question: Opening WIP R20 000, total manufacturing cost R450 000, closing WIP R30 000. Cost of production of finished goods is…
Which is NOT part of the Production Cost Statement?
questions.memo: Office salaries are administration, not production cost.

questions.question: Factory overheads include indirect materials and indirect labour.
questions.memo: Overheads are the indirect factory costs.

questions.question: Classify each cost.
questions.memo: Materials, labour and overheads each have their place.

questions.question: If closing WIP is higher than opening WIP, the cost of finished goods is…
options: Lower than the total manufacturing cost
Higher than the total manufacturing cost
questions.expected: Lower than the total manufacturing cost
questions.memo: More value stays in WIP, so finished-goods cost is lower.

questions.question: The Production Cost Statement is supported by ______ for each cost.
questions.memo: Notes detail each cost.

questions.question: Total cost of production divided by units produced gives the…
questions.memo: Unit cost = total cost ÷ units.

questions.question: The Production Cost Statement is prepared by a manufacturing business.
questions.memo: It applies to manufacturers.

questions.question: Direct labour is the wages of…
questions.memo: Direct labour makes the product.

questions.question: Why prepare a Production Cost Statement?
options: To calculate the cost of goods manufactured for the period
questions.expected: To calculate the cost of goods manufactured for the period
questions.memo: It establishes the manufacturing cost.

questions.question: Raw materials consumed = opening raw materials + purchases −…
questions.memo: Consumed = opening + purchases − closing.

ACC.G12.T3.COSTANALYSIS.A1.title: Unit costs, break-even & cost control
ACC.G12.T3.COSTANALYSIS.A1.description: Preparing a short-form Income Statement with notes for administration and selling & distribution cost, calculating gross profit on finished goods sold, variable and fixed costs, cost per unit, contribution per unit and the break-even point, and interpreting the results.
ACC.G12.T3.COSTANALYSIS.A1.recovery_strategy: Above break-even = profit; below = loss. Compare units produced/sold to the break-even units to judge whether the business covers its costs.

questions.question: Break-even is the point where total income equals total…
questions.memo: At break-even, income covers all costs.

questions.question: Selling price − variable cost per unit = ______ per unit.
questions.memo: This is the contribution per unit.

questions.question: Cost per unit = total cost ÷…
questions.memo: Unit cost = total cost ÷ units.

questions.question: Fixed costs R100 000 and contribution per unit R25. Break-even units are…
If the business produces above its break-even point, it makes a…
questions.memo: Output above break-even earns profit.

questions.question: Sort each cost as fixed or variable.
questions.memo: Fixed costs stay constant; variable costs change with output.

questions.question: A short-form Income Statement separates…
options: Cost of sales, administration and selling & distribution costs
questions.expected: Cost of sales, administration and selling & distribution costs
questions.memo: It splits the main cost categories.

questions.question: Gross profit on finished goods sold = sales −…
questions.memo: Gross profit = sales − cost of sales.

questions.question: Producing below the break-even point results in a ______.
questions.memo: Below break-even, costs exceed income.

questions.question: Selling price R40, variable cost R24, fixed costs R80 000. Break-even units are…
questions.memo: Contribution R16; R80 000 ÷ R16 = 5 000 units.

questions.question: Lowering the variable cost per unit lowers the break-even point.
questions.memo: Higher contribution means fewer units to break even.

questions.question: If the unit cost rises but the selling price stays the same, profit per unit…
questions.memo: A higher cost with the same price shrinks the margin.

questions.question: Sort each cost as administration or selling & distribution.
questions.memo: Office costs are administration; getting goods to customers is selling & distribution.

questions.question: A business producing 6 000 units with break-even at 5 000 units is…
questions.memo: Output above break-even earns profit.

questions.question: To improve profit, a business can raise the selling price or lower the ______ cost.
questions.memo: Reducing unit cost widens the margin.

questions.question: Contribution per unit first covers fixed costs, then becomes…
questions.memo: After fixed costs, contribution is profit.

questions.question: Comparing actual unit cost to the budgeted unit cost is a control measure.
questions.memo: Variance analysis controls costs.

questions.question: If the break-even point is very close to actual output, the business has…
questions.memo: Little buffer above break-even is risky.

questions.question: Why calculate the cost per unit?
options: To set prices and judge profitability
questions.expected: To set prices and judge profitability
questions.memo: Unit cost guides pricing and profit decisions.

questions.question: Why interpret cost information?
options: To control costs and improve profitability
questions.expected: To control costs and improve profitability
questions.memo: Interpretation drives cost control.

ACC.G12.T3.BUDGETING12.A1.title: Budgeting: analysis & interpretation
ACC.G12.T3.BUDGETING12.A1.description: Analysing, interpreting and comparing Projected Income Statements and cash budgets for sole traders or companies (receipts, payments, debtors' collection, creditors' payment and cash balances), and comparing budgeted to actual figures as a control.
ACC.G12.T3.BUDGETING12.A1.recovery_strategy: Compare budget to actual and ask WHY. Underspending on maintenance or wages may signal neglect, not good control.

questions.question: A cash budget plans future…
questions.memo: It plans cash in and out.

questions.question: Comparing the budget to the ______ figures is a key control.
questions.memo: Budget-to-actual comparison controls performance.

questions.question: A favourable variance means actual results were…
questions.memo: Favourable = better than plan.

questions.question: A Projected Income Statement forecasts future profit.
questions.memo: It estimates the expected profit.

questions.question: Actual wages were far below budget. This might mean…
options: Understaffing or a genuine saving — investigate why
questions.expected: Understaffing or a genuine saving — investigate why
questions.memo: Variances should be investigated, not assumed good.

questions.question: Compare two businesses' budget control.

source_a.text: Source A: compares actual to budget monthly and acts on variances.

source_b.text: Source B: prepares a budget but never checks actual results.

statements.text: Uses the budget as a control tool
Gains little control from its budget

questions.memo: A controls with the budget; B's budget is unused.

questions.question: If actual sales are below budget, the business should…
options: Investigate the reasons and take action
questions.expected: Investigate the reasons and take action
questions.memo: Shortfalls need investigation and action.

questions.question: A cash budget helps a business avoid running out of ______.
questions.memo: It anticipates cash shortfalls.

questions.question: A favourable variance is not always good because…
options: It may hide neglected spending, such as on maintenance
questions.expected: It may hide neglected spending, such as on maintenance
questions.memo: Underspending can signal neglect.

questions.question: Budget-versus-actual comparison helps managers control performance.
questions.memo: It is a core control technique.

questions.question: Depreciation appears in a Projected Income Statement but not in the…
questions.memo: Depreciation is non-cash.

questions.question: Compare projected and actual results.

source_a.text: Source A: actual profit matched the projection closely.

source_b.text: Source B: actual profit was far below the projection.

statements.text: Suggests over-optimistic budgeting or poor performance
Compares a projection with the actual result

questions.memo: A's budget was realistic; B's large gap needs investigation.

questions.question: An unfavourable variance on expenses means actual expenses were…
questions.memo: Unfavourable expense variance = overspend.

questions.question: Drawings appear in the cash budget as a ______.
questions.memo: Drawings are cash paid out.

questions.question: A business that consistently misses its sales budget should…
questions.memo: Persistent misses call for review.

questions.question: A cash budget surplus means receipts exceeded payments.
questions.memo: A surplus means more cash in than out.

questions.question: Why compare actual results to the budget?
options: To control performance and correct problems
questions.expected: To control performance and correct problems
questions.memo: Comparison enables control and correction.

questions.question: Spending far less than budgeted on repairs may signal…
options: Neglected maintenance, not necessarily good control
questions.expected: Neglected maintenance, not necessarily good control
questions.memo: Underspending on upkeep can be a warning.

questions.question: Projected receipts from debtors depend on the collection ______.
questions.memo: Collections follow how fast debtors pay.

questions.question: The main purpose of budget analysis is to…
options: Control costs, plan cash and improve performance
questions.expected: Control costs, plan cash and improve performance
questions.memo: It supports control and improvement.
